launches.tagline: Meet Praxis AI, the platform made to eliminate fire-fighting for manufacturing engineers
launches.body:
# TL;DR

Praxis AI builds manufacturing-specific agents capable of reasoning and processing complex situations. Our engineering copilot predicts and prevents machine failures in real-time by solving problems the same way an engineer would. This results in proactive maintenance which helps prevent unplanned downtimes and quality defects.

[Launch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJ41WG_X8pw):

# The Problem

We have over 10 years of experience working in the manufacturing industry between the two of us. During that time we have noticed that manufacturing engineers are constantly being pulled in every direction due to production issues popping up in multiple parts of the plant. 

This reactive approach results in:

* Large amounts of unplanned downtime, resulting in lost throughput
* Unnecessary wear and tear on expensive manufacturing machinery
* Quality defects requiring non-value add rework prior to customer delivery

From unplanned downtimes alone, US manufacturers lose over **$50 billion dollars per year**. \
\
Unfortunately, existing solutions are:

* Complex and required large amounts of data science/computer science knowledge
* Focused on dashboarding and KPI metrics
* Extremely costly to implement and maintain
* Not tailored for manufacturing use cases

# The Solution

Praxis AI provides manufacturing engineers with an end-to-end solution for identifying and root-causing machine issues by following a 5-step reasoning process. This mimics exactly how an engineer would solve an issue in the real world. Our platforms core competencies include:

1. **SOTA AI architectures for manufacturing** - Our models have been specifically designed to work with time series data coming from the manufacturing shop floor.
2. **No code tools for manufacturing engineers** - The Praxis AI platform can be used without ever touching a Jupyter notebook.
3. **Explainable AI for root cause analysis** - Our UI gives users full visibility into the reasoning behind the output of our models, and our copilot Max.e.
4. **Operationalized machine learning models** - Praxis ensures that every model that is built is able to be utilized every single day to drive actual changes on the shop-floor. It's not just a pretty dashboard to look at.

The Praxis platform provides the tools needed for engineers to make changes on their shop-floor which can lead to reductions in unplanned downtimes, reduced scrap/waste, improvements on the efficiency of their machines, and so much more. We’ve built the platform in a way that as we continue to work with more customers, we will be able to encompass more and more use cases. We’ve already begun preliminary work on adding production order optimization and maintenance backlog management to our solution suite. 

# The Team

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=85869&key=user_uploads/2229645/e65c1855-0e3c-4b5a-9014-22f633580153)

We have been working in the manufacturing industry for our entire professional career, and are extremely passionate about being on the cutting edge of manufacturing technology.

Ransika has worked at multiple manufacturing companies like GM, Tesla, and Rockwell Automation. During this time he has worked a variety of foundational manufacturing roles like manufacturing engineer, quality engineer, controls engineer, and production planner. During this time he managed multiple projects building and implementing various digital manufacturing projects globally which resulted in millions of dollars in cost savings per year. For the last two years he has been working at Deloitte as a product lead for Deloitte’s Intelligent Ops platform.

Aditya worked at Palantir for three years, ending his career there as a technical lead. During this time he specialized in converting pilots in the manufacturing vertical with a 100% success rate and a TCV of over $15 million dollars. Aditya has had a passion for ML/AI in manufacturing since early college, first excelling in the space by building a predictive model for General Motors and winning first in a data challenge of over 50 teams of PhD and masters students.

# Our Ask

If you are interested in testing our solution out, we would love to be in touch to do a free factory assessment! We are looking to test our solution in a variety of different manufacturing environments, but have a particular affinity to continuous processes that can be found at paper mills, oil refineries, and chemical plants. Feel free to reach out at [founders@praxis-tech.ai](mailto:founders@praxis-tech.ai). Thanks!

launches.title: Sift: The Anti-Logging Platform
launches.tagline: Sift is the AI-driven engine transforming chaotic streams of observability data into valuable intelligence. Transform chaos into clarity. Leave the logs behind.
launches.body:
**Sift** transforms your logs from overwhelming chaos to clear, powerful insights. Our platform profiles, analyzes, and routes your logging data, intelligently eliminating noise and highlighting critical data. Continuously learning and adapting, Sift evolves with your data to keep you ahead of every challenge.

<https://youtu.be/wwV51eEy59s>

## **How We Got Here**

While seeing band aid logging products launched at both Datadog and Splunk, we witnessed firsthand how traditional logging tools overwhelm developers with data—burying critical insights under mountains of noise. Teams waste countless hours sifting through logs, missing the signals that matter most. Meanwhile, costs escalate as volumes grow, and early decisions limit vendor flexibility. We realized the problem wasn't just about collecting logs but in really understanding them.

Frustrated by these limitations, our mission for Sift became clear: create an anti-logging platform that gives developers control over their data while unlocking its true potential.

## **Sift through your data, intelligently**

<https://youtu.be/uQ-TTdiu3fc>

Sift is designed to flip the script on traditional logging. We’re not here to simply collect logs; we’re here to transform them into actionable intelligence that empowers developers and drives smarter decision-making.

1. **Profile, analyze, and continuously optimize** your logging data to find meaningful patterns without digging through mountains of information.
2. **Send your logs** exactly where they need to go, integrating right into your existing tooling
3. **Format and manage** your log volume precisely to focus on the information that matters most.

## **How Sift Works**

**Quick Setup:** Launch Sift with minimal configuration—start sending data in minutes.

**Seamless Integration:** Connect effortlessly with your existing logging infrastructure, with support for over 40 different integrations

**Dynamic Adaptation:** Our system continuously learns from your logs, optimizing rules and suggesting smart routing—like sending low-value logs to cost-effective storage solutions.

launches.title: Morphik: Open‑source multimodal RAG that works on technical docs
launches.tagline: Turn your complex private data into grounded answers
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋 We’re Adi and Arnav, co-founders of Morphik (https://morphik.ai).

### **TL;DR**

* **Problem:** Knowledge workers spend a lot of their time searching complex documentation with diagrams, tables, or spreadsheets, just to find relevant information. Text‑only RAG misses details, hallucinates, and provides half-baked responses.
* **Solution:** Morphik embeds whole pages (image + text, no OCR), auto‑builds a knowledge graph, and serves it through a UI, SDK, or REST API. We have 90 % accuracy on arXiv QA (and we can fine-tune for your use case 🙂).

Watch our demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3adZQhm5JZY

### **Problem**

RAG breaks the moment documents stop being blobs of text.

* Knowledge workers spend a lot of their time (people we spoke with said 50-70% time just in the research phase). eg. electrical engineers finding perfect PCB spec, pharma companies trying to search ELNs for similar experiments.
* 80% of enterprise knowledge lives in diagrams, tables, images, CAD, scanned pdfs, not .txt.
* “Multimodal” models still hallucinate or miss key context because the retrieval step sees only text, or they rely on tools to retrieve diagrams, or context. (https://docs.morphik.ai/blogs/gpt-vs-morphik-multimodal)
* Teams glue together OCR, vector DBs, and regex‑heavy ETL that becomes a brittle monstrosity.

### **Solution**

Directly embedding and search over page images

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdzvQJeEBmnvZI1Mkl2ZYCtsN0AG4Mx5JpcN4RtivMfndGshgTkj1uZcb8BkFAkXXNCpg9TPqeIKsqCXscaLzGDNO2e8TFn8naJPkJ_XtceDHlwNrAAcV69QGYlzSOwvdofI7FksQ?key=wmYsqYRKzN1ploJFaFpgwCeu)

When you ingest in Morphik, in addition to OCR, we create direct embeddings for the image of a page (or frames in a video). When you ask “Colpali comparison to standard RAG”, the LLM sees the actual page image, so multimodal models can reason over arrows, labels, scales, and colours just like a human.

### **Rules Engine**

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcOXXa3wTpZV26zi8kaucVOt2QuUgKKfrdvlyqlFfeHmDUudWpNaS-r6KNm5--4Joz4rE5tsiu_NDqlHnRE914l7ad4YtKRRLc_X1gm7BteBR0aMN446aia7LGA1l7b2UJMor97?key=wmYsqYRKzN1ploJFaFpgwCeu)

When ingesting, you can define rules for data extraction (which would again consider tables, diagrams), or define natural language rules for PII redaction, or content transformation.

### **Deployment ready, scalable**

Morphik comes built in with folder scoping, end user scoping, GPU accelerations, and fine grained permissions, so you can prototype and deploy with enterprise grade features. It’s end‑to‑end, so you don’t scramble to make duct tape fixes.

### **One more thing…Morphik Research Agent**

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcL9LvkrH861vRDhuFlYlBy0LsjlhMOYVBLRLdnj903G5L3QMgx12ziGZJhO_h2SzAakjD27e0Yeu4XZwmsE4Yv1BGNRj-OGc41i798xy_UW9MVHISzJy0GBrTsOWWqWBGdtGKhmg?key=wmYsqYRKzN1ploJFaFpgwCeu)

Our research agent uses Morphik’s retrieval, graph, and extraction APIs as tools. It chains them automatically, jumping from doc to doc, node to node, seeing figures, till it finds the needle in the haystack, or has enough context to answer your questions. “Describe the third pin on the USBC21 diagram” will get the diagram, find the pin, jump to the table with pin descriptions, jump to page 13 to “find more details on page 13”.

### **Why we might be interesting to you**

* Building an internal ChatGPT over messy manuals? Morphik is the fastest way to ship something users _trust_.
* Developing an AI product? Swap your vector‑DB‑plus‑duct‑tape stack for a single SDK call.
* Researching graph‑RAG? CAG? We have it all.

### **Our Ask 🙏**

1. **⭐ Star / watch** https://github.com/morphik-org/morphik-core – open source momentum matters.
2. **Introductions** to teams drowning in technical docs (healthcare, manufacturing, legal, electrical engineers).
3. Tell us **what still hurts in your RAG stack**, comment, **DM, or email** [founders@morphik.ai](mailto:founders@morphik.ai) or [book a call](https://cal.com/adityavardhan-agrawal-x6jyhq/30min).

Thanks for reading!

Adi & Arnav

launches.title: Castari – The runtime for agents that need a computer
launches.tagline: Your agent executes code, calls tools, and runs for hours. We give it a sandbox, an endpoint, and observability — with one command.
launches.body:
### TL;DR

Castari is hosting infrastructure for agents that need more than an API call. Run `cast deploy` and your agent gets a secure sandbox, auto-scaling endpoint, and full observability.

Public beta is live today.

<https://youtu.be/2fpCTj051kY>

---

### The problem

Serious agents aren’t just “call an API and done.”

They execute code, hit tools and browsers, run for minutes to hours, and touch sensitive systems. Every team ends up rebuilding the same fragile setup:

* homegrown agentic harnesses
* stitched-together sandboxes/microVMs/containers/queues
* logs and traces scattered everywhere
* hacky snapshots and suspect secret handling

So:

* every agent needs its **own** mini-runtime
* debugging one run is detective work
* adding a new agent feels like starting a new infra project

Deploying agents that work great locally turns into wrangling infrastructure.

---

### **The problem**

Serious agents aren't chatbots. They execute code, call tools, touch filesystems, and run for hours. They need a computer.

But there's no good way to put them in production. You end up stitching together containers, queues, and compute layers — rebuilding the same infrastructure every team rebuilds. The agent works on your laptop. Getting it to work reliably for users takes weeks.

We hit this ourselves. We built an AI consumer app to 2M+ members while at RunPod (scaled to $100M revenue). The hardest part was never the model — it was the harness. Every time we shipped a new agent, we were rebuilding sandboxing, scaling, secrets, and monitoring from scratch.

### **What we built**

Castari wraps your agent in a secure sandbox and gives you back a production endpoint.

```
npm install -g @castari/cli
cast login
cast deploy
```

Your agent now has:

* **Secure sandbox** — full isolation. Your agent can safely execute code, use browsers, and access filesystems
* **Auto-scaling endpoint** — scales with demand, no capacity planning
* **Observability** — trace every tool call, decision, and output in real time
* **Multi-model support** — Claude, OpenAI, xAI, open source. Your code stays the same
* **Zero lock-in** — remove Castari and your agent still runs on vanilla Claude Agent SDK

---

### **How we're different**

Most tools give you primitives — a sandbox API, a container runtime, a compute layer. You still stitch it together yourself.

Castari wraps around your agent. You define it declaratively, we manage the lifecycle: provisioning, versioning, execution, scaling, teardown. You write agent logic, not infrastructure code.

### **What's next**

* Better tracing and observability — debug agent behavior in production, not after the fact
* Higher sandbox concurrency limits — run more agents in parallel
* Forever-running sandboxes — agents that stay alive indefinitely

---

### Why we’re working on this

While I was leading the FDE team at RunPod:

* Built and shipped AI infrastructure and agents for **Fortune 500s and fast-growing startups**
* Watched the same loop repeat: agent works in a notebook → weeks disappear into infra glue → nobody trusts the system, production release gets delayed (over and over again).

Additionally, while [@Cambree Bernkopf](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1372064) and I scaled our AI consumer app to 2m+ users, our biggest issues were getting our agents to work reliably in production.

The pattern is clear: **agents deserve a first-class runtime, the way frontends got one.**

Castari is our bet that:

* Sandboxing & safety should be built-in, not bolted on
* Going from “prototype” to “production-safe” should be one config file, not a quarter-long project
* AI teams should ship agents, not infrastructure.

---

### Try it

Docs: [docs.castari.com](http://docs.castari.com)

Website: [castari.com](http://castari.com)

CLI: `npm install -g @castari/cli`

Or email [jacob@castari.com](mailto:jacob@castari.com) — happy to get you deployed.

— Jacob & Cambree

launches.body:
Hey! We’re Jacob Wright & Cambree Bernkopf, founders of [Castari](https://castari.com).

### **TL;DR**

**Castari lets teams deploy AI agents to secure, autoscaling sandboxes in seconds.**

You write agent logic with the **Claude Agent SDK (other frameworks coming soon)**. We turn it into a production-grade endpoint.

We’re especially focused on:

* Teams building **internal agents** (ops, support, data, eng workflows).
* Companies whose **core product is an agent** built on Claude Agent SDK and need a safe, reliable way to run it.

### Launch Video:

https://youtu.be/81K80OivtAc

### The Problem:

Serious agents are not just a single API call. [Agents need a computer.](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk)

They execute code, call tools and browsers, run for minutes instead of milliseconds, and touch sensitive systems. Most teams end up rebuilding the same fragile setup:

* Homegrown agent harnesses
* Sandboxes, file systems, and queues stitched together
* Logs and traces scattered across many services
* Ad hoc snapshots and risky secret handling

The result:

* Every agent needs its own mini runtime
* Debugging one agent run feels like detective work
* Adding a new agent feels like starting a new infra project

Good agents stall at “cool demo” instead of reaching production. Deploying agents becomes a full-time infrastructure problem.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95573&key=user_uploads/89898/44917ba7-819c-4c41-a80f-ef359054b19e)

### How Castari solves it

We’re building Castari to be the **natural runtime for AI agents built on Claude Agent SDK**. We wrap the entire agent in a sandbox, deploy it, and provide you with an endpoint url that auto-scales as requests come in. No need to write code in your tools to manage your sandbox lifecycle.

#### **1. Drop in a config file → get a production runtime**

In your Claude Agent SDK repo:

* Add a `castari.yaml` (entrypoint, tools, env vars)
* Run `castari deploy`

That’s it. Your agent is now running in a secure sandbox with an endpoint, UI, and observability.

Whether that agent is:

* an **internal system** your team uses
* a **customer-facing agent** that _is_ your product

the deployment workflow is identical and boring (in the good way).

#### **2. Sandboxing & safety, built-in**

* Every run executes in an isolated sandbox designed for tool-using agents
* You design the behavior; we handle isolation and scaling
* No more duct-taping together sandbox primitives for specific tools

**Bottom line:** You keep building on **Claude Agent SDK** the way you already are — for internal workflows or core products. Castari turns that into a safe, observable, production-ready runtime.

### Why Castari is different

**E2B, Modal, Daytona, Cloudflare** (and friends) give you powerful sandbox and compute primitives.

**Castari sits one layer up:**

Castari wraps around your Claude Agent SDK-based agents so you can define them declaratively and run them in secure sandboxes, without owning the underlying sandbox lifecycle.

* **Agent-first semantics**: runs, sessions, tools, snapshots are native concepts we manage.
* **Zero framework lock-in**: remove Castari and your agent still runs on vanilla Claude Agent SDK; keep Castari and your infra team gets its life back.
* **Focused start**: deeply integrated with **Claude Agent SDK** today, with the same “drop-in config” experience coming to other frameworks next.

We’re building the runtime we wish existed for agents.

### Why we’re working on this

While I was leading the FDE team at RunPod:

* Built and shipped AI infrastructure and agents for **Fortune 500s and fast-growing startups**
* Watched the same loop repeat: agent works in a notebook → weeks disappear into infra glue → nobody trusts the system, production release gets delayed (over and over again).

Additionally, while [**@Cambree Bernkopf**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1372064) and I scaled our AI consumer app to 2m+ members, our biggest issues were getting our agents to work reliably in production.

The pattern is clear: **agents deserve a first-class runtime, the way frontends got one.**

Castari is our bet that:

* Sandboxing & safety should be built-in, not bolted on
* Going from “prototype” to “production-safe” should be one config file, not a quarter-long project
* AI teams should ship agents, not infrastructure.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95573&key=user_uploads/1070542/5fbe422a-1cc4-49e3-95ce-8740164b600e)

### Ask: early pilot access

We are opening a limited pilot for:

* Teams building internal agents who need a safer, more reliable runtime
* Companies building agent centric products that need to run in production without bespoke infra

If that is you and you are tired of wrestling with sandboxes, observability, and brittle tooling:

→ Email [**jacob@castari.com**](mailto:jacob@castari.com) with subject “Castari Pilot” and 2 to 3 sentences about your agent stack and use case.\
→ Check out our open source repo for using any model with Claude Agent SDK on [GitHub](https://github.com/castar-ventures/castari-proxy).\
→ Join the waitlist on [**castari.com**](http://castari.com) to hear about our first releases.

Jacob, Cambree, and the Castari team

launches.tagline: 2025 Tariffs Megathread
launches.body:
Hey Everyone!

Excited to share our story and what we’ve been working on.

https://youtu.be/kdNXKa-zfcg

When Chan worked on Tesla’s Global Trade team, every car part—bolts, batteries, doors, etc—came from a different country. Each time tariffs shifted (pretty frequently), he and his team had to manually check thousands of parts across hundreds of pages of trade rules. Pair that with meetings with consultants, brokers, & suppliers to get potentially the worst workflow of 2025. All happening within Outlook & Excel 2019.\
They tried software, consultants, startups — every one of them got shot down due to reasons like product quality & data security, but mainly that it doesn’t bring enough value.

That’s why we built **MarkIt** — AI agents that actually _do the work_ for Suppliers, Brokers, and OEMs.

# **Introducing MarkIt - The Silver Bullet for Trade Compliance**

With agents that live where trade professionals already work — **Excel, broker portals, and browser** — MarkIt helps teams classify products, manage tariffs, and resolve customs issues in seconds, not hours.

# **MarkIt’s Value: Product & Logic Application**

MarkIt is intentionally lightweight, and customizable. Previously, without AI, software in this industry was clunky & typically automating a set workflow. Now, MarkIt services all of your workflow needs in a single

* **Classification**: MarkIt can enhance your workflows at scale. Entries are

  **defensible** with thorough **reasoning** and **supporting documents**.
* **OCR**: Upload your Bill of Ladings, Commercial Invoices, Packing Lists, and other documents to create your import filings and reports.
* **Customization**: Users can choose to **use their own logic**, where MarkIt’s platform would simply handle applying it at volume. No more worrying about reasonable care, if you don’t trust AI research.
* **Build Your Own:** MarkIt’s agents can work in files & desktop, applying trade logic in your own customizable way.
* **Integration:** Plug directly into ABIs and ERPs **only if you want.**

MarkIt is like a coworker specialized in customs & the trade process. Who’s willing to do all of your mindless “dishwashing” work.

# **Our Ask:**

We’re looking to connect with anyone who works in Global Trade. Suppliers, customs brokers, manufacturers, e-commerce operators, etc.

Chan: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chanhkim/)

Roland: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rsaav/)

launches.title: EigenPal: AI Document Workflows
launches.tagline: EigenPal automates enterprise document processes with AI
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** EigenPal automates your document processing workflows with AI. If you have humans reading documents and typing data into systems - KYC docs, invoices, claims, shipping forms, contracts, receipts - we replace that. Works on messy scans, handwritten forms, third-party docs. Beautiful workflow builder, testing, and team functionality. On-prem ready or use our cloud. Working with 2 large European banks on loan automations already.

Try on: [**eigenpal.com**](http://eigenpal.com)

**2 minute demo -** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pEfhqhylS2Y>

**What We Learned**

Working on back office document automation, we kept hearing the same questions:

* _"How do I know this workflow will actually work before I bet my ops on it?"_
* _"I aim to have 100 workflows. How will I monitor them all?"_
* _"Can this run in our cloud? Data can't leave our infrastructure."_
* _"Our files have contracts, amendments, and extensions that reference each other. Can you piece that together?"_

Traditional automation tools were built for deterministic processes and they're not designed for AI. AI is a game changer for document processing, but businesses still can't trust it at scale. Why? Evals and monitoring aren't built in. And most new platforms can't run on-prem.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97202&key=user_uploads/2221380/d651a1db-2002-456e-9c18-55d290083745)

**The Solution: A Platform Where You Can Trust AI Workflows**

EigenPal is built around one principle: like any employees you entrust work to, you need to trust your workflows before you deploy them and monitor them after.

* **Agentic workflow builder.** Our AI workflow builder let’s you create workflows with easy in your natural language. It can even iterate on a workflow on a test dataset to tune accuracy.
* **Eval-first.** Before any workflow goes live, test it against your historical documents. See exactly what accuracy you're getting. Deploy only when you're confident. **Set up a feedback loop in production** so workflows are adjusted with feedback.
* **Document-centric.** Upload files directly, no public URLs needed. Built-in storage plus a powerful template filler to generate polished output docs from your extracted data.
* **Configure everything.** Choose your OCR/VLM, LLM, configure every step of the pipeline separately. Access built-in tracing for workflows in our app or export via OpenTelemetry.
* **Monitor hundreds of workflows at once.** One dashboard showing costs, compliance logs, and failures across every workflow. Know immediately when something drifts.
* **Collaborate with your team.** Org workspaces let you share workflows, templates, and results with colleagues. Build once, use across your team.
* **On-prem or cloud.** Runs in your infrastructure with your LLMs, or use our hosted version. Your choice.

launches.body:
**MochaCare** ([mochacare.com](http://mochacare.com)) unlocks home care agency growth with human virtual assistants supercharged by AI. We take hiring, scheduling, or both off agencies' plates so they can spend less time drowning in ops and more time building relationships in their communities. \
\
Everything we do generates data insights that surface growth opportunities, from referral leads to sales enablement during intake calls.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98296&key=user_uploads/570409/6292e9a2-6ebc-4f33-9cf0-1e60f6c1ca3f)

\* Note: a home care agency is a company that hires and manages caregivers on behalf of people seeking care. These caregivers typically work with clients in their homes or in facilities.

We personally embed into the agencies we work with. Our AI hiring and scheduling agents handle most tasks for us, but we are always monitoring the feed and jumping in if emergencies arise.

Nick goes to bed at 3:30am and Pranav wakes up at 3:30am to guarantee 24/7 coverage.

**What problem are you solving?**

1. **Home care agency operators** want to deliver quality care to their communities, not to stay glued to their phones 24/7 handling hiring and scheduling. They’re burning out and are unable to grow their businesses.
2. **Families** want reliable care. They need to know that the best caregivers are going to show up for their loved ones at the right time and need home care agencies to be energized so they can deliver their best care. Scheduling and hiring mishaps erode the quality of care and cause service failures for these families.
3. **Caregivers** want work quickly and don’t want to deal with manual data entry. They needed their next paycheck yesterday. Our hiring agents (including AI interviewers and interview coordinators) get them through the process swiftly. Once hired, they need to know about the best shifts for them. Our scheduling agents alert them to these and help them focus more on care and less on manual tasks like shift note entry.

**Why are you working on this?**\
We were both raised by our grandparents who gave the world to us. We want to live in a world where they receive the same quality care and attention that they gave us growing up. Currently, there’s a gap between that world and where we are today.

We’ve seen this first-hand. Home care operations can fall short—Nick’s grandma recently started receiving home care and had no caregiver show up on day one. We don’t want this to happen again.

On the other side of the equation, we’ve seen agency owners with the largest hearts feel hopeless about their work. We want to uplift these people and allow them to reclaim their time, get back to delivering care, and start growing their agencies.

By helping agencies deliver care more effectively, we protect the superheroes who care for our communities and the people who they care for, like our grandmas!

**Our ask:**\
Intros to home care agencies, home health agencies, or anyone who advises seniors on care options (since these people typically know home care agencies).

Thank you for taking the time to read this!

launches.title: Trellis: Autonomous Agents for Short Term Rentals
launches.tagline: Run all your operations end to end across every tool in your stack.
launches.body:
Hi, we’re [Lodovico Benvenuti](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lodovico-benvenuti-11678224a/) and [Jan Sahagun](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jan-sahagun-escosa?utm_source=share&utm_campaign=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=ios_app), and we’re building Trellis, AI agents that run operations for short-term rental property managers.

Our Launch Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zki0_icE3Xw>

### The problem

Short-term rental operations break as companies scale.

As you add listings, coordination explodes across guest messaging, cleaning, maintenance, and homeowners. Work ends up spread across 5 to 10 disconnected tools, duck-taped together by burnt-out teams, constantly firefighting issues, with information inevitably falling through the cracks.

Quality drops, reviews follow, and growth stalls.

This is because managing a property is complex. Let’s say the guest calls about a broken shower. The operator has to identify the reservation in the PMS, search a separate knowledge base for context, collect photos, and create a task in another system.

Then check a workforce tool for availability, reprioritize tasks, dispatch a technician, follow up with the guest, and later log costs, update accounting, and notify the homeowner. All this across 5-10 systems of record.

The core issue is simple: no software has full operation context to control operations end to end.

### What we built

Trellis provides AI agents that run operations across the entire stack.

The agent communicates with guests, dispatches and coordinates cleaners and maintenance, files claims and costs, and follows up until issues are fully resolved.

It connects to PMSs, messaging channels, and internal tools, but more importantly, it maintains full operational context: who the guest is, what property they’re in, what the issue is, what’s already been tried, who is available, what tasks are in progress, and what needs to happen next.

Instead of passing information between tools, the agent owns the entire workflow from first message to resolution and reporting.

When agents take over operations, execution becomes consistent and verifiable. That shifts control of the guest experience from marketplaces back to operators, who can now deliver reliable service at scale, build real brands, and own demand.

### Our background

Before Trellis, Lodo built AI customer service agents for short-term rentals at Conduit (YC W24). He also scaled a property management company to \~$2M revenue and 150+ listings. With trellis we are now running their operations with 1 person.

Jan spent years in the trenches of the STR industry: leading early sales at multiple AI tools for property managers, building an STR tech media platform (STR Tech Report), consulting across the space, attending 20+ industry events, and speaking with thousands of property managers along the way. That journey earned him deep trust and relationships throughout the STR world.

---

If you run a property management company, we’d love to show you Trellis.

launches.tagline: AI voice agents for enterprise contact centers running on legacy phone infrastructure
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We are Haithem and Chehir - co-founders of  [Callab AI](https://callab.ai/). 

**The problem**

The global call center industry is worth $400B, and about 58% of it still runs on on-prem PBX infrastructure like Cisco UCM, Mitel, and FreeSWITCH. These systems have been in place for 20 years, with millions invested in deploying and maintaining them. They work, and they're not going anywhere.

AI voice agents have been built on top of cloud telephony providers, which means every solution on the market today requires the customer to already be on cloud phone systems. If you're running on-prem, you're locked out. The only option is a full migration to cloud, which typically takes 12 to 18 months, costs a fortune, and frequently fails. Meanwhile, these same companies are dealing with 30 to 40% agent attrition rates, rising labor costs, and customers who won't tolerate hold times. They want automation but they simply can't access it.

That's a massive segment of a $400B market sitting there with no solution available to them.

**What we built**

Callab AI is a cloud-based AI voice platform that connects directly to on-prem PBX systems via SIP trunk integration. The phone system stays exactly where it is, calls get routed to our AI agents, handled, and returned. No rip-and-replace, no migration, and we go live in one week.

We automate up to 70% of inbound call volume across use cases like call routing, appointment scheduling, order status, and customer inquiries. The hard part is the integration layer itself, which requires going deep into legacy telecom infrastructure that most teams don't want to touch. We built it to work with any telephony stack, and that's what makes this possible.

We're YC P25 and currently expanding into the US, focused on hospitality, logistics, retail chains, and property management. Healthcare and financial services are on the roadmap once we complete HIPAA compliance.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101754&key=user_uploads/1938837/5d95733e-2ac9-45b4-8f2b-5ef8a8a3b8ca)

**How we got here**

We didn't set out to become the on-prem PBX company. We started building AI voice agents in the Middle East and Africa, where cloud telephony providers don't operate, SIP trunks are state-regulated, and every contact center runs legacy infrastructure. We had no choice but to build our integration layer to work directly with whatever phone system was already on the ground. After plugging into old telecom stacks, we realized the problem we solved out of necessity in MEA is the exact same problem sitting untouched in the US. The constraint that shaped our product in a harder market turned out to be a global advantage.

**How you can help**

If you know anyone at a company running a legacy phone system or on-prem contact center, we'd love an intro. Hotels, restaurant groups, logistics operators, large retail, or property management are all ideal. Also happy to connect with anyone who's worked with managed service providers, value-added resellers, or sold into enterprise telecom IT. Drop me a note.

launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋**

I'm Justin, founder of Sidekick.

**TL;DR** Sidekick is an AI assistant that frontline manufacturing workers use over text message. They text a number and it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes work orders, and syncs with the software the company already uses. No app, no login, no training. I built Sidekick for my dad's manufacturing shop. It’s now live at facilities across the globe.

**_Ask:_** Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility? I'd love an intro! Email [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick).

Check out our launch video:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxwq5ZAojXg>

## ❌ The Problem

I grew up in my dad's manufacturing plants and spent summers working on the factory floor at EDS Manufacturing.

Here's what I watched happen repeatedly. A machine goes down, everyone's waiting, and the person who can help is in a meeting or on another line. Half the time the answer already existed. Nobody could get to it.

Why it keeps happening:

* **No computer access.** Nobody on that floor has a company login or an email address, so none of the plant's software reaches them.
* **The answers are scattered.** An SOP in a binder, a manual on a shared drive few have permissions to, a safety procedure someone printed and taped to a wall in 2019.
* **The best answers were never written down.** Thirty years of tribal knowledge lives in one guy's head, and when he retires it leaves with him.
* **So the same questions get asked over and over.** Shift after shift, and every one of them costs somebody their afternoon.

There are 239,000 manufacturing plants in the US, and only 29% of the people working in them have advanced digital skills. Any tool that requires a download, a login, and training makes adoption difficult.

## ✅ Our Solution

Workers text the Sidekick phone number. Problems, photos, voice memos, in any language. No app to download, no account to create, nothing to learn. Every worker on the floor already knows how to send a text, which is why adoption isn't a fight.

* **Answers from your own documents.** SOPs, manuals, safety procedures, tribal knowledge. Sidekick responds in the worker's language, in seconds.
* **Creates and routes the work order.** The issue gets logged and sent to the right person, without anyone needing a laptop.
* **Syncs with the software you already run.** Sidekick pulls from and writes to your existing systems instead of replacing them, and integrates directly through PLC and SCADA systems so the floor and the software finally see the same thing.
* **Captures tribal knowledge.** Every exchange builds a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so the know-how stays when the veteran leaves.

Here's a full walkthrough:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a5zBRSXi-90>

## 👤 The Team

I'm Justin, founder and CEO. I'm the third generation in a manufacturing family, and I've been around plant floors since I was a kid. I studied Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, worked in finance at Arm, and left both to build Sidekick after watching the same problem play out on every floor I'd been on.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you answer "yes" to any of these, I'd love your help:

* **Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility?** Even a name and a "you two should talk" goes a long way.
* **Have you sold software into manufacturing?** I'd love to hear what actually worked and what didn't.

Contact me at [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick)**.**

### **TL;DR**

Walter is an AI employee for the manufacturing back office. Instead of building yet another integration, we gave Walter a login. He signs into SAP, Microsoft Dynamics 365, or Oracle the way a new hire would, works out of Teams and email like the rest of the team, and takes over the manual work no one wanted: entering purchase orders, ordering from suppliers, catching pricing errors before they ship. A purchase order that used to take 15 minutes now takes a few seconds.

### **The Team**

* Nikolas Keller grew up across four countries, started to cook in French, Italian and German fine dining kitchens at 18, then flew to San Francisco with a duffel bag and talked his way into a manufacturing AI startup backed by Neo & GC.
* Lukas Postulka paid for TU Munich by living in a monastery in exchange for cleaning. Got a job at  PwC by mailing them a portfolio they never asked for. Landed a job as quant trader by scoring first on technical trial.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102405&key=user_uploads/3097279/555d91df-f392-4137-ae2a-d5816f70df7b)

### **The Problem**

We talked to more than 100 manufacturers and heard the same story every time. For thirty years, every vendor sold them the same fix and none of it worked.

* Better integrations, cleaner APIs, a newer ERP: all sold as the answer, none of them the problem.
* The real bottleneck was never the software. It was that a person had to sit there and operate it, one purchase order at a time.
* So the back office stays buried in manual data entry, supplier emails, and pricing mistakes caught too late.

The work is repetitive, high volume, and expensive to staff. Every factory has it. No one has solved it.

### **Our Solution**

We stopped trying to replace the software. We gave Walter a login instead.

Walter logs into the systems a factory already runs (SAP, Dynamics, Oracle, Teams, Outlook and Gmail, etc.) the way a new employee would. Same screens, same buttons, no integration project, no rip and replace. He reads the orders, enters them, places supplier POs, and catches the pricing mismatch before it becomes a costly mistake. 

What used to take a back office team now runs on its own.

We start with packaging and industrial manufacturing, where the ERPs are oldest and the manual load is heaviest. The endpoint is bigger: once Walter runs the workflows, the software underneath becomes a database he operates in.

### **Our Ask**

If any of these are you, we'd love to talk:

* Manufacturers drowning in back-office data entry across SAP, Dynamics, or Oracle.

* Anyone who knows a factory still doing this work by hand.

**TL;DR:**[ Modern](https://getmodern.ai) is consolidating the IT function into a single platform powered by secure agents who understand your business. **The problem**

We've spent over a decade buying and implementing clunky IT software (ServiceNow, Jira SM, Ivanti, Zendesk), staffing internal teams, and paying expensive MSPs to keep operations running. Seb previously co-founded Frankie/Unmind, Europe's leading digital mental health company (used by Disney, Uber, Lendlease, Standard Chartered, and the MLB). Aleks has been building developer platforms and scaling engineering teams at Wix and Canva, including Wix's first low-code platform.

Today's ITSM platforms take months to implement, need weeks to design rigid automations, can't improve over time, and have always been hard to leave.

So we asked: what would this stack look like if it were AI-native from day one?

\
**What is Modern**

An all-in-one secure IT function, Modern splits reasoning from actions which enables the unlock for secure AI in IT.

* Requests are made in the tools where your team works → Slack, Teams, email, voice, WhatsApp, Telegram.
* Agents reason about each ticket, and the actions they take are separate, code-based workflows derived from your SOPs, written in natural language, or installable skills you approve.
* Every interaction feeds Modern to better understand your IT operations so automation coverage compounds over time.

Modern is for you if:

* The Engineering or Operations teams are handling your IT requests
* IT tickets pile up faster than your team can clear them
* Access requests crawl through approval chains (manager → Finance → IT → resolved a week later)
* On/off-boarding is manual, error-prone, and takes time
* Compliance and audit prep means stitching logs together from a dozen disconnected tools

launches.title: Kebra — Making the field queryable
launches.tagline: We capture what happens in field operations and turn it into the context AI employees need to automate the work that follows
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋

We’re [Luca](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luca-hadife/) and [Hosny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohamed-hosny-hussein/), founders of [Kebra](https://kebra.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026).

## TL;DR

Kebra makes the field queryable.

We capture what happens across jobs, sites, and assets and turn it into a live operating memory that AI can query and act on. Our AI employees use that context to automate the work that follows across the systems companies already use.

Every job makes that memory richer, building the company specific context software agents use today and physical agents will need tomorrow.

We’re already working with field operations companies across Florida, Pennsylvania, and California.

<https://youtu.be/VIwv5iVm8Ok>

## The problem

Field operations never got their Claude Code moment.

We spent months inside HVAC companies trying to automate their back office. We built AI employees for claims, reporting, coordination, and follow ups.

They kept breaking.

Not because the AI could not do the work, but because it was acting on a reality that never happened. The most important part of the operation happened on the ground and was never properly captured.

A missing serial number. A photo never taken. What the technician actually found stuck in their head.

You cannot automate an alternate reality. Before AI can operate the field, the field has to become queryable.

## Our Solution

Kebra makes field operations queryable.

**Capture what happens:** Field teams document jobs through photos, voice, video, and structured workflows. Kebra checks what is missing while they are still on site.

**Build the operating memory:** Every job updates a live history of sites, assets, repairs, decisions, and how the company actually works.

**AI employees act on it:** They use that context to automate reports, claims, coordination, compliance, follow ups, and other back office work across the systems the company already uses.

## Vision

Every job makes Kebra’s operating memory richer.

Today, software agents use that context to automate field operations. Tomorrow, physical AI and robots will need the same company specific context to understand each site, asset, procedure, and history before they can work autonomously.

Kebra is building the context layer for field operations.

## Our Ask

Run or know a company with field operations where important information gets lost between the field and the office?

Email us at [founders@kebra.com](mailto:founders@kebra.com) and [book a demo](https://calendar.app.google/s1DwDxHTbxZ9w5Uq6).\
Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kebra-com)

launches.tagline: Run every repair from first call to first-time fix.
launches.body:
**Bernard is building the AI front and back office for home and commercial appliance servicers.**

They manage each repair from the first customer call through scheduling, dispatch, diagnosis, parts preparation, technician handoff, and follow-up. Bernard works across phone, text, email, warranty feeds, and existing field-service systems, carrying the job context across every surface.

We are already live in the field with some of the largest authorized service companies in the country.

Our goal is simple: make the first visit the last one.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eiGjkYMeu2k>

### The first truck roll should not be a diagnostic visit

Appliance repair is an information and inventory problem. A technician cannot simply carry washer parts. The exact appliance, model, revision, symptoms, and failure mode determine which parts might be required, and many nearly identical parts are not interchangeable.

When that information does not come together before the appointment, the first visit becomes a diagnostic visit. The technician identifies the failure, orders the part, and returns days later to complete the repair. Customers wait longer, technicians complete fewer jobs, and servicers lose capacity and margin.

### Pre-ID prepares the repair before the truck rolls

When a customer reports that their washer will not drain, Bernard does more than book an appointment.

Bernard identifies the exact appliance, asks follow-up questions specific to the symptoms, and collects missing evidence from the customer. Pre-ID then combines that information with repair history, similar completed visits, manufacturer guidance, parts data, and the servicer’s own operating knowledge.

Before the visit, Bernard gives the technician a diagnosis, ranked parts, the most useful next questions, and the evidence supporting each recommendation. The office can prepare the parts, confirm they will arrive on time, and hand the technician a complete picture of the job.

Every interaction and completed repair feeds back into Bernard, turning the servicer’s daily work into shared knowledge.

### Why start with the servicer?

Every appliance company makes a promise at the point of sale. The servicer is the person who ultimately has to keep that promise inside someone’s home or business.

That visit affects the customer, the retailer, the manufacturer, the warranty company, and the parts distributor. Yet the servicer coordinating it is often working across disconnected phone systems, inboxes, scheduling tools, parts catalogs, and knowledge held by a few experienced employees.

We believe that building the world’s most efficient appliance servicers will create happier customers and a more connected appliance ecosystem.

Bernard starts with the servicer because that is where the industry meets the physical world.

### About us

[Dan Katzman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dankatzman/) previously helped build Nava Benefits' strategy and operations team, working across the product and operational infrastructure required to deliver a complicated, service-heavy experience reliably, while also leading partnerships. Before Nava, he invested at City Light Capital and Golub Capital.

[David Goodfellow](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dgoodfellow/) grew from product engineer to engineering manager at Radar Labs, where he led fraud and geo-compliance products and helped replace the incumbent provider at DraftKings and Bet365. Before that, he worked on RPA and cognitive automation at Disney, before enterprise automation was cool.

### Talk to us

If you run an appliance service company or lead service operations at an appliance manufacturer, retailer, warranty company, or service network, reach out to us at [founders@bernardhq.com](mailto:founders@bernardhq.com)

launches.title: Zaplar - Replacing PMS and the Hotel Tech Stack.
launches.tagline: Replacing the fragmented hotel tech stack with one system that can understand and run hotel operations.
launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Axel, Oscar, Jon, and Douglas, founders of Zaplar.

**TL;DR:** Zaplar is an agentic hotel OS that replaces the fragmented hotel tech stack (PMS, booking engine, channel manager, POS, revenue management, housekeeping, and more) with one system built from the ground up for AI. We're eight people with backgrounds in hotel operations, engineering, AI research, and cybersecurity.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/c7720ef9-5a08-43eb-9631-4fefb2d239b6)

**Ask:** Intros to hotel owners and operators who are unhappy with their PMS, and to executives and C-suite at hotel groups planning their next core system replacement. Details at the bottom. Reach us at [founders@zaplar.com](mailto:founders@zaplar.com).

[Launch Video!](https://youtu.be/bpfJATRnYQM)

## The problem

Incumbents are bolting AI onto systems built for a different era. They provide a layer of AI to the end user, but the automations beneath it stay constrained. Their claim to use AI is correct. They just can't reason across the operation or automate work end to end.

No existing PMS or bolt-on solution gives hotels the architecture AI actually requires. And even if one did, a PMS alone still wouldn't automate hotel operations. It's one of as many as 15 systems a hotel runs, each built on a different architecture, each focused on one part of the operation, none able to act beyond its own boundaries.

AI can't run a hotel if it can't understand the hotel.

To unlock the full potential of AI, a hotel has to run on a single system with a unified architecture: one that lets AI reason across the entire property, free of the boundaries integrations create and the context each one isolates behind them. Incumbents can't build this without replacing the foundation their business depends on, and they won't.

We arrived at this the slow way. Douglas's family has spent their careers running hotels, and we first built Zaplar to solve event bookings for them. In demo after demo, hotels were already evaluating another PMS, including ones that had just switched. Even leading vendors did not make a product hotels wanted to use.

## The solution

Zaplar was built on this thesis from the start: the first truly AI-native operating system for hotels. It’s the path of most resistance, but the only way to do it right.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/5a0f8f2c-bcb0-4ebc-a3e1-e2c30c80baec)

Zaplar spatially maps out the entire property and its resources so that AI agents can reason across the hotel and understand how everything connects. On top of this architecture sit a PMS, POS, channel manager, booking engine, guest portal, housekeeping system, and more, with no boundaries between them. The result is an autonomous system that works in the background and completes work on its own. The system surfaces suggestions for staff to review, edit, and approve.

Our goal is to be vertically integrated. Beyond deeper automation and richer context, the greatest benefit is that we can put all our effort into staying at the forefront, because we're not constrained by what anyone else is doing. Major hotel groups are starting to replace their aging systems, and we intend to be the only option on the table designed for what comes after.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/ad3b8b01-9f05-41f1-877e-952a35dc8e8a)

## Our ask

**Hotel owners and operators.** If you own or operate a hotel that is unhappy with its PMS, we would love to talk directly.

**Executives and C-suite at hotel groups.** This is the intro we want most. Anyone at the VP level or above at a group, especially COOs, CIOs, CTOs, and heads of operations or commercial, and above all anyone whose group is planning a core system replacement in the next 18 months.

**Everyone else.** You do not need to know their software situation to make the intro useful. We are focused on independents, small and mid-size groups, and boutique and luxury properties. If you have stayed somewhere you loved, send us the name and we will take it from there.

Reach us at [founders@zaplar.com](mailto:founders@zaplar.com) or learn more at [zaplar.com](http://zaplar.com).

launches.title: Cerenovus - The Layer between Data and Decisions
launches.tagline: AI that finds the money your company is losing
launches.body:
TL;DR: We made an AI system that reads through a company's information (communications, documents, databases - whatever they want to analyze) and finds concrete, actionable steps they can take to improve their business and make it more efficient.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SxuAHO3-0WEjPPqZUkK-39jWfitRvlQj](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SxuAHO3-0WEjPPqZUkK-39jWfitRvlQj/view?usp=sharing)

**The Product** 

Large companies are extremely complex systems. As soon as a company scales past fifty or so employees, it becomes totally impossible for an executive to know every single thing that happens at a company. This means that, since everyone at a company only understands a small slice of what's going on, it's essentially inevitable that inefficiencies arise on a global level that aren't visible at smaller scales. Before Cerenovus, this was a very difficult problem to tackle, because there was just too much information for any one person to have the whole picture. Cerenovus changes this.

**Here's how Cerenovus works:**

First, Cerenovus ingests the company's information. This looks differently for every company based on their priorities and existing systems, but typically this means hooking into documents, communications and databases that the company wants to analyze, and bringing all the information together in one place.

Next, Cerenovus runs an AI-powered synthesis pipeline to organize the information and map out all existing systems and workflows. Once the system has mapped out how things work at a company, it scans for a wide variety of common failure modes, and does open-ended analysis to find places where processes can be streamlined. Finally, its findings are compiled into polished, cited briefs, reviewed and validated by humans, and then shipped back to our clients.

We're looking to sell to any business interested in optimizing their business, making sense of information, and leveraging AI to the greatest extent possible. However, the people that can use our product the most are the ones that do this kind of optimization repeatedly: private equity value creation teams, exit planners, and operational consulting firms.

**The Lore**

We're three ex-Harvard nerds who were brainstorming in a library one night, and found that we were all (in different ways) interested in the problem of knowledge organization. Jonathan was obsessed with building out a personal "second brain" for himself in Obsidian; Ollie had worked on building agent harnesses that could self-improve by updating their internal knowledge base; and Lucas had seen how, whenever a company got acquired by the private equity firm he worked at, people within the company didn't have the full picture of how work got done. We decided to leave school and build our idea together, and the months since have been a blur of coding, conferences, and customer calls.

**The Ask**

We'd love to be connected to:

\- Private Equity Value Creation Teams

\- Exit Planners

\- Operational Consultants

\- Innovative middle-market businesses looking to improve their operations

**We’re disrupting the disruptors.**

You’ve heard of so many AI accounting startups already. These new “AI-native” accounting firms are still designed to be run by humans in two facets: the first 25%, fostering client relationships, and the final 25%, signing off and filing with the IRS.

**Josh Kushner’s company, Thrive Holdings, the largest disruptor in this space, explicitly argues that agents will never replace this** \[1\]**.** Their reasoning? Agents don’t carry trust.

Currently, agents are not trusted, humans are. That’s why every AI startup nowadays does the work, and leaves judgment to a human. But this is changing, and we’re early. As new agent-centric companies grow (Instinct, Natural, AgentMail), agents become common in daily life and work, and eventually will become trusted entities \[2\].

Once agents are trusted, there is no reason they cannot own entire, traditionally trust-heavy industries, end-to-end. Rational is building for that world.

**Reach out to [founders@rational.to](mailto:founders@rational.to) or visit [rational.to](http://rational.to) if interested in learning more.**

---

\[1\] <https://www.thriveholdings.com/long-humans>. A fraction of the market does care about trust and the human relationship with their accountant, but most of us definitely do not want to spend a second more with one than we have to.

\[2\] These companies inherently bet on agents to proliferate in society. We also believe AI will continue to get better and safer. Since trust is achieved through consistent, positive actions, and it is in the interest of the entire tech industry for their agents to produce consistent positive actions, our firm will be the first to enjoy the principles to do concrete work in a massive market.

name: Sona8
long_description:
Sona8 is a voice agent that talks to every employee about how their work gets done. Consulting, transformation and corporate development teams spend a large part of every project on stakeholder interviews and stakeholder alignment, and still only hear from a small share of the people affected.

Each employee gets a link and talks to the agent for about 20 minutes. The agent asks follow-up questions, for example why a step is still done by hand or who else is involved. From the conversations we build process maps and a list of the problems people described, by site and team.

During the implementation, the agent goes back to the employees involved after each initiative and asks whether it was implemented and what changed. The result is a project management office that has talked to every employee. Today consulting firms buy it for the stakeholder interviews at the start of an engagement. Transformation and corporate development teams buy it to run the implementation of a change program.

Over time this becomes the way a company knows how it runs. Sona8 reads the systems the company already uses, connects them to what employees said, and keeps the picture current by asking again. Before a decision, you ask what it would do across sites and teams and get an answer from the whole company. A small team steers a company-wide program that used to need a large one. And AI agents inside the company come here first to learn how the work is done before they change anything.
one_liner: Voice agents that talk to employees enabling transformations

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: Thilo and I worked on the same consulting project. We did over 70 stakeholder interviews, then had to manage the stakeholders  during implementation, which meant aligning the same people over and over. In the nights we went running a lot in that time. On one of those runs we started asking what if we automated the whole thing. An AI would be strictly better at every step. It asks better questions because it has heard the other interviews, it analyzes with all the context, and it can go back a month later and ask again.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every big decision in a company is a choice between alternatives. The alternatives you see depend on the context you have. The context that matters most, how the work is done and where the problems are, sits with thousands of employees and never reaches the people who decide.

If we succeed, that context reaches them. Every employee talks to Sona8, and Sona8 plugs into the ERP, the HR system and the ticketing tools. Together that is a live map of how the company runs, and far more than any team can read. The hard part is finding, out of all of it, what matters for one question, and then adding the atomic insights and the judgment. This way, transformation, strategy and consulting teams operate far leaner and faster. Three people steer a program across 20,000 employees.

On top of the map we build a synthetic layer of employees. Before a decision, you run it against that layer and see what it does across sites and teams.

The same map is the enterprise context layer for AI agents. Before an agent changes a process, it reads how that process is done today and by whom. Sona8 is where that map lives.
